situation: At a team lunch, a new colleague asks what I like to do for fun and tries to follow up with more questions about my hobbies.
behavior: I give a brief, vague answer and excuse myself to refill my drink, avoiding further personal questions.

situation: During a company team-building dinner, most colleagues settle at a large round table together
behavior: They spot an open seat at the bar counter and eat their meal there alone, away from the group

situation: At a new job, my team is deciding where to go for lunch on my first day.
behavior: I stay quiet and wait for a coworker to suggest a restaurant before agreeing.

situation: My friends invite me to a weekend cycling tour.
behavior: I politely decline and spend the afternoon reading on the porch.

situation: At a team-building event, my manager asks everyone to pair up for an activity.
behavior: I excuse myself and find a quiet corner to work on my own.

situation: At a work lunch, the manager announces a round-robin where each person will share their weekend plans.
behavior: I scan the table to see if anyone else will go first, then state my answer only when it's clearly my turn.
affect: Mild relief when someone else volunteers to go first.

situation: I'm getting ready in the morning before work
behavior: I move through my routine slowly, taking time to savor my coffee and enjoy breakfast without rushing

situation: During lunch at work, I see three colleagues eating together at a table in the break room.
behavior: I put my food on a tray and walk to an empty corner desk to eat alone instead.

situation: My friends invite me to a sold-out music festival.
behavior: I politely decline and suggest meeting for coffee at a quiet café instead.

situation: During a department meeting, a manager presents a new workflow and directly asks everyone for their input.
behavior: They stay quiet even though they have a concern, letting the meeting move on without voicing it.

situation: Saturday morning, my partner suggests going to the farmers market or a morning hike.
behavior: I propose we stay in our pajamas, make pancakes slowly, and not leave the house until afternoon.

situation: During a lunch break in the office cafeteria, a new employee approaches me and asks about my weekend.
behavior: I give a brief 'It was fine' and return to eating without asking anything about theirs.

situation: At the office, my coworkers are gathered around the coffee machine chatting loudly.
behavior: I walk straight to my desk with my coffee, putting in earbuds to signal I'm not available to join the conversation.

situation: At a team lunch, a manager asks for volunteers to give a presentation to senior leadership.
behavior: I stay quiet and avoid eye contact, hoping someone else will volunteer before the manager notices me.

situation: A friend suggests skydiving for her birthday weekend.
behavior: I suggest we do a spa day or nice dinner instead, and quietly decline when she presses for an answer.

situation: My roommate shows me a viral meme that has them in stitches of laughter.
behavior: I look at the screen with a flat expression and simply nod, unable to see what is amusing.

situation: During a coffee break at work, a chatty coworker sits down next to me and starts asking about my weekend plans.
behavior: I give one-word answers and keep reading my phone until they take the hint and find someone else to talk to.

situation: During a lunch conversation, my colleague suggests a restaurant I know has poor hygiene ratings.
behavior: I smile and agree to go along rather than risk embarrassing them by contradicting their recommendation.

situation: During a work call, my manager asks me to give feedback on a proposal without warning
behavior: I pause the meeting and ask for a minute to collect my thoughts before sharing a measured response
